id: ax_indemnity_burn
statement: "A memory taken under co-op indemnity is taken whole: the person cannot recover it, and cannot be told it without the telling being logged."
scope:
  - memory
  - law
  - indemnity
  - co-op
consequences:
  - "Ilan cannot recover the read-key seating sequence by any effort of his own"
  - "Anyone who tells him commits a logged offence and the co-op learns who"
  - "His hands may still hold what his memory does not, because procedural skill is not indemnified"
exceptions:
  - "Physical habit is outside the indemnity and is not taken"
cost: "the teller's certification, and the co-op's attention"
---

An indemnity is how a co-op pays for an injury it does not want valued. The injured member
is compensated, and in exchange the co-op takes the memory of the work that caused the
injury - not the fact of the injury, and not the years around it, but the procedure itself,
lifted out entire. What is taken is taken whole. There is no fragment left to worry at, no
edge to catch on, no version that comes back under pressure. The member is not confused
about the past; the past simply has a shape in it where a procedure used to be.

The burn is enforced by the log rather than by the surgery. Anyone may in principle say the
thing out loud, and the saying is a recorded offence against the indemnity, chargeable to
the speaker's certification. This is what makes the burn hold in a habitat of forty people
who all know each other: it is not that nobody could tell him, it is that telling him costs
the teller everything and the co-op finds out within the shift.

What the indemnity does not reach is the body. A splicer's hands keep a seating sequence the
way they keep a knot, below the level where anything was ever put into words, and the co-op
has never claimed that ground because claiming it would make every indemnified member
useless. So the man cannot tell you what he did. Put him in front of the work and his hands
can still do it, and neither he nor anyone watching will be able to say how.
